title: A stiff back
context: A 38-year-old man has had years of morning back stiffness that eases with exercise. He also had a red, painful eye last year.
question: What's the diagnosis?

img.author: Stevenfruitsmaak
img.alt: Thin, smooth bony bridges (syndesmophytes) join the vertebrae into a continuous column

hints: Look at the shape of the spine: smooth, joined-up edges.
The vertebrae have fused into one long column that looks like a plant stem.
why: Thin, smooth bony bridges (syndesmophytes) join the vertebrae into a continuous column: a 'bamboo spine'.
assoc: Inflammatory back pain in young adults
pearl: Inflammatory back pain improves with exercise and is worse with rest and in the early morning. Treat early: modern biologics can prevent fusion.

title: Dull on one side
context: A 41-year-old with weeks of cough, night sweats and weight loss is now breathless. One lung base is dull to percussion.
question: What's the diagnosis?

img.file: Pleural effusion of primary pulmonary tuberculosis.jpg
img.author: Basem Abbas Al Ubaidi
img.alt: A dense white opacity at the left base with a curved upper edge rising towards the side wall (meniscus sign), obscuring the diaphragm

hints: The white area hides the diaphragm and the costophrenic angle.
Its upper edge curves up at the side, like a meniscus.
why: A dense white opacity at the left base with a curved upper edge rising towards the side wall (meniscus sign), obscuring the diaphragm: a pleural effusion, here from tuberculosis.
pearl: Tap it if you don't know why it's there. Light's criteria separate exudates from transudates. In many countries, TB is a leading cause of exudative effusion in young adults.

title: A fall on the hand
context: A 72-year-old woman slipped on wet tiles and landed on her outstretched hand. Her wrist looks like a dinner fork.
question: What's the diagnosis?

img.author: Lucien Monfils
img.alt: A fracture of the distal radius with the broken fragment angled backwards (dorsally)

hints: The break is in the radius, just above the wrist.
On the side view, which way has the broken end tipped?
why: A fracture of the distal radius with the broken fragment angled backwards (dorsally): the 'dinner fork' deformity of a Colles fracture.
pearl: A low-energy wrist fracture in an older person is often the first sign of osteoporosis, so consider bone density testing. A Smith fracture tips the other way (forwards).

title: Recurrent infections
context: A 58-year-old woman has had repeated urinary infections and loin aches. Plain X-ray of the abdomen:
question: What's the diagnosis?

img.author: Nevit Dilmen
img.alt: A large, branching radio-opaque stone filling the renal pelvis and calyces of one kidney, shaped like a stag's antlers.

hints: There's a large white, branched shape over one kidney.
It fills the renal pelvis and branches into the calyces, like antlers.
why: A large, branching radio-opaque stone filling the renal pelvis and calyces of one kidney, shaped like a stag's antlers.
assoc: Struvite stones from urease-producing bacteria (e.g. Proteus)
pearl: Staghorn calculi are usually infection stones and can destroy the kidney if left. They usually need removal (often percutaneous nephrolithotomy) plus treatment of the infection.

title: A child's elbow
context: A 7-year-old fell off the monkey bars onto an outstretched hand and won't move the elbow.
question: What's the diagnosis?

img.author: James Heilman, MD
img.alt: A fracture across the lower humerus just above the condyles, with some displacement of the lower fragment.

hints: Look just above the elbow joint, at the lower end of the humerus.
Compare the alignment of the humerus with the capitellum.
why: A fracture across the lower humerus just above the condyles, with some displacement of the lower fragment.
assoc: Fall on an outstretched hand in children (5–7 years)
pearl: The commonest elbow fracture in children. Always check the radial pulse and nerves (especially the anterior interosseous nerve: ask for an 'OK' sign). A raised posterior fat pad suggests a hidden fracture.

title: A bad flare
context: A 29-year-old woman with known ulcerative colitis has bloody diarrhoea, fever, a racing pulse and a tender, swollen abdomen.
question: What's the diagnosis?

img.author: Hellerhoff
img.alt: Marked dilatation of the colon (transverse colon over 6 cm) with loss of the normal haustral pattern, in a systemically unwell patient with colitis

hints: The large bowel is very dilated, especially the transverse colon.
Put the X-ray together with fever, tachycardia and her known bowel condition.
why: Marked dilatation of the colon (transverse colon over 6 cm) with loss of the normal haustral pattern, in a systemically unwell patient with colitis: toxic megacolon.
pearl: Toxic megacolon is a surgical emergency with a high risk of perforation. Avoid opioids, antidiarrhoeals and anticholinergics, and involve surgeons early.

title: Coughing for months
context: A 45-year-old with a cough.
question: What's the diagnosis?

img.author: CDC
img.alt: Patchy shadowing in both upper zones with a thick-walled cavity at the right apex

hints: Where the disease sits matters more than the hole itself: look at both upper zones.
Bilateral upper-zone shadowing plus a thick-walled apical cavity: think of the oldest infectious killer.
why: Patchy shadowing in both upper zones with a thick-walled cavity at the right apex: classic post-primary (reactivation) TB.
pearl: Upper-lobe cavitation means a high bacterial load: isolate the patient and send three sputum samples. TB remains one of the world's leading infectious killers.

title: A puffy face and dark urine
context: A 12-year-old had a sore throat three weeks ago. Now he has puffy eyes, cola-coloured urine, high blood pressure and is breathless.
question: What's the diagnosis?

img.author: CDC/Dr Thomas Hooten
img.alt: An enlarged heart shadow with congested lungs (fluid overload) in a child with haematuria, oedema and hypertension weeks after a strep throat

hints: The heart looks big and the lungs look congested.
Put it with the sore throat three weeks ago and the cola-coloured urine.
why: An enlarged heart shadow with congested lungs (fluid overload) in a child with haematuria, oedema and hypertension weeks after a strep throat: acute post-streptococcal glomerulonephritis.
assoc: Group A streptococcal throat or skin infection
pearl: An AP film exaggerates heart size, so be careful calling cardiomegaly on it. Post-strep GN is still common in remote Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander communities, often after skin sores.

title: Fell off his bike
context: A 30-year-old came off his bike onto his shoulder. He has a tender lump over the front of the shoulder.
question: What's the diagnosis?

img.author: Majorkev (cropped)
img.alt: A break through the middle third of the collarbone with the ends slightly displaced.

hints: Follow the long bone across the top of the chest.
There's a break in its middle third.
why: A break through the middle third of the collarbone with the ends slightly displaced.
pearl: Most mid-shaft clavicle fractures heal well in a sling. Check the skin over it and the neurovascular status of the arm; shortening, skin tenting or an open wound needs a surgical opinion.

title: Vomiting and a swollen belly
context: A 66-year-old who had bowel surgery years ago has colicky abdominal pain, vomiting and hasn't passed wind for a day.
question: What's the diagnosis?

img.author: Igboeze
img.alt: Multiple dilated, centrally placed bowel loops with air-fluid levels in a 'step-ladder' pattern

hints: Look for stacked loops of bowel with horizontal lines across them.
The dilated loops are central and the lines are air-fluid levels.
why: Multiple dilated, centrally placed bowel loops with air-fluid levels in a 'step-ladder' pattern: small bowel obstruction.
pearl: Adhesions cause most small bowel obstructions in people who've had surgery; hernias are the main cause in those who haven't. Always check the hernial orifices.

title: Puffing on the stairs
context: A 71-year-old man with 40 pack-years of smoking is breathless on stairs and breathes out through pursed lips.
question: What's the diagnosis?

img.author: James Heilman, MD (cropped)
img.alt: Lateral chest X-ray showing a barrel-shaped chest, large retrosternal space and flat diaphragm

hints: This is a side-on film. Check the shape of the chest and the line of the diaphragm.
The chest is barrel-shaped, the air space behind the breastbone is large and the diaphragm is flat.
why: Lateral chest X-ray with a barrel chest, a wide retrosternal air space and a flattened diaphragm: the signs of hyperinflated, damaged lungs.
pearl: The diagnosis of COPD comes from spirometry, not the X-ray, which can be normal in mild disease. Stopping smoking helps more than any other step. Smoke from indoor cooking fires is a major cause in women in low-income countries.

title: Two months of cough
context: A 64-year-old woman who has never smoked has had a cough for two months and has lost 5 kg without trying.
question: What's the diagnosis?

img.author: Δρ. Χαράλαμπος Γκούβας (Harrygouvas)
img.alt: Frontal chest X-ray with arrows around a large irregular mass in the left mid and upper zone

hints: Follow the arrows, then ask what the edge of the shadow looks like.
An irregular, poorly defined mass in someone losing weight is the worry here, not infection.
why: A large, irregular, ill-defined mass in the left mid and upper zone, outlined by the arrows. There is no air-fluid level or lobar air bronchogram to suggest abscess or pneumonia.
pearl: Up to about a quarter of lung cancers worldwide occur in people who have never smoked, and many are women with adenocarcinoma. A cough lasting more than three weeks deserves a chest X-ray, and a normal film does not fully exclude cancer if worry persists.

title: Off the skateboard
context: A 29-year-old fell onto an outstretched hand from a skateboard and now has a swollen, deformed forearm and a painful wrist.
question: What's the diagnosis?

img.author: Th. Zimmermann
img.alt: Two views of the forearm showing a displaced distal radial shaft fracture and disruption at the wrist

hints: Find the bone that is broken, then check the joint at the far end of the forearm.
The radius is broken in its lower third and the joint between radius and ulna at the wrist has come apart.
why: Two views show a displaced fracture of the distal third of the radial shaft, with dislocation of the distal radioulnar joint at the wrist. The ulna itself is intact.
pearl: A memory aid for the two look-alikes is MUGR: Monteggia breaks the Ulna, Galeazzi breaks the Radius. In adults this injury is unstable and usually needs surgical fixation, and every forearm fracture needs the wrist and elbow on the film.

title: Slow to walk
context: A 2-year-old who was exclusively breastfed without vitamin D drops and gets little sun has been slow to walk and has thick wrists.
question: What's the diagnosis?

img.author: Frank Gaillard
img.alt: X-ray of both hands and wrists of a young child with cupped, frayed metaphyses at the distal radius and ulna

hints: Look at the ends of the radius and ulna, just before the growth plates.
The metaphyses are widened and cup-shaped, with fuzzy edges instead of a crisp line.
why: Cupping, splaying and fraying of the distal radial and ulnar metaphyses, with a widened gap to the small epiphyses. Unmineralised growth plate is failing to calcify properly.
pearl: Nutritional rickets is preventable and still common worldwide. Risks include darker skin, covered clothing, little sun, and breastfeeding without a vitamin D supplement. Treatment is vitamin D with enough calcium, and the X-ray changes usually heal.

title: After the crash
context: A 34-year-old motorcyclist has left-sided rib and shoulder-tip pain after a road crash. Pulse 110, blood pressure holding.
question: What's the diagnosis?

img.author: Hellerhoff
img.alt: Axial contrast CT of the upper abdomen with an irregular dark cleft in the spleen

hints: Compare the solid organs: liver, then the organ at the back on the right of the image.
There's an irregular dark cleft in the lower part of that organ, after a blow to the left side.
why: Contrast CT in the portal venous phase shows an irregular low-density cleft in the spleen, which should enhance evenly, consistent with a traumatic tear.
pearl: Stable patients are often managed without surgery, sometimes with embolisation, and unstable patients go to theatre. After splenectomy, people need vaccines against encapsulated bacteria and a clear plan for fever.

title: A fall in the bathroom
context: A 78-year-old woman slipped in her bathroom and can't stand. Her leg looks short and turned outwards.
question: What's the diagnosis?

img.author: Booyabazooka
img.alt: X-ray of the hip with a blue arrow at a displaced fracture of the femoral neck

hints: Follow the arrow to the bone just below the ball of the hip.
The break sits between the head and the trochanters, inside the joint capsule.
why: A displaced fracture through the femoral neck, just below the head, with the shaft shifted upwards. The break is above the trochanters, inside the capsule.
pearl: Aim for surgery within 48 hours, with good pain relief and early walking. About one in four people die within a year, so a hip fracture also calls for bone health treatment and a falls review.

title: Green vomit on day one
context: A newborn, whose antenatal scan showed too much amniotic fluid, starts bilious vomiting within hours of birth.
question: What's the diagnosis?

img.file: Double-Bubble-Zeichen bei Duodenalatresie und Pancreas anulare 1tW - CR ap - 001.jpg
img.author: Hellerhoff
img.alt: Abdominal X-ray of a newborn with two large gas-filled bubbles in the upper abdomen and no distal bowel gas

hints: Count the gas-filled shapes in the upper abdomen.
There are two large bubbles side by side, and no gas beyond them.
why: Two gas-filled structures, the stomach and the dilated first part of the duodenum, with no gas further down: the classic double bubble. In this baby surgery also found an annular pancreas.
pearl: About a third of babies with this condition have trisomy 21. Green vomit in a newborn is a surgical emergency until proven otherwise, because malrotation with volvulus can look similar and can cost the baby their bowel.

title: A veil over one side
context: A 67-year-old long-term smoker has had weeks of cough and breathlessness, and has now coughed up a little blood.
question: What's the diagnosis?

img.author: Hellerhoff
img.alt: Frontal chest X-ray with a veil-like haze over the left upper chest and mediastinal shift to the left

hints: Compare the density of the two sides, then see where the trachea and mediastinum sit.
A hazy veil over the upper left chest that fades downwards, with volume loss rather than a fluid level.
why: A veil-like haze over the left hemithorax that fades towards the base, with volume loss: the mediastinum is pulled to the left and the lobe has collapsed forwards against the front of the chest.
pearl: In an adult smoker, lobar collapse is an obstructing central cancer until proven otherwise, so it needs CT and usually bronchoscopy. The left upper lobe collapses forwards, which is why it looks like a veil rather than a wedge.

title: New breathlessness
context: A 63-year-old man having chemotherapy through a port under his collarbone has become breathless over a few weeks.
question: What's the diagnosis?

img.file: Lungenmetastasen bei Pankreaskarzinom im Roentgenbild des Thorax 001.jpg
img.author: Hellerhoff
img.alt: Frontal chest X-ray with many round nodules of varying size in both lungs and a chest wall port

hints: Count the lesions, then look at their shape and where they sit.
Many round, soft-tissue nodules of different sizes, more in the lower lungs where blood flow is greatest.
why: Countless round, well-defined nodules of varying size through both lungs, heavier at the bases, spread by the bloodstream. This man's primary was pancreatic cancer. A chemotherapy port is also visible.
pearl: Blood-borne deposits collect at the lung bases because that's where most blood goes. Large 'cannonball' deposits are classically seen with kidney, colorectal and germ cell cancers. Miliary TB nodules are tiny and all the same size.

title: Aching and tired
context: A 70-year-old has aching in the forearm, tiredness and recently worsening kidney function.
question: What's the diagnosis?

img.author: Hellerhoff
img.alt: X-ray of the forearm and elbow with multiple punched-out holes in the bones

hints: Run your eye down the shafts of both forearm bones and into the humerus.
Multiple round holes in the bone, punched out and without a dense rim around them.
why: Multiple sharply defined, punched-out lytic lesions along the radius, ulna and distal humerus, with no surrounding sclerosis.
pearl: Isotope bone scans can miss these lesions because bone-building activity is suppressed, so low-dose whole-body CT or MRI is preferred. Think of this diagnosis in an older person with unexplained anaemia, kidney impairment or back pain.

title: Off the horse
context: A 23-year-old woman fell from a horse, landing on her outstretched forearm. The elbow and forearm are swollen.
question: What's the diagnosis?

img.author: Hellerhoff
img.alt: Long X-ray of the forearm showing a proximal ulnar fracture and a dislocated radial head

hints: Find the broken bone, then look at the joint nearest the elbow.
The ulna is broken in its upper part, and a line along the radius no longer hits the capitellum.
why: An angulated fracture of the proximal ulna with dislocation of the radial head at the elbow.
pearl: A line drawn down the shaft of the radius should pass through the capitellum in every view. The dislocation is easy to miss when the fracture draws your eye, which is why every forearm film should show the joints at both ends.

title: Hot knee, sudden onset
context: A 76-year-old woman has a suddenly hot, swollen, painful knee, and no fever.
question: What's the diagnosis?

img.author: Taokinesis (Pixabay profile) Annotated by Mikael Häggström
img.alt: Frontal X-ray of the knee with arrows marking thin white calcification in the joint space

hints: Look where the arrows point, within the joint space itself.
There's a thin white line inside the cartilage where there should be nothing visible.
why: Thin calcification within the meniscal cartilage on both sides of the joint, marked by the arrows. Calcium pyrophosphate crystals are deposited in the cartilage and can trigger acute flares.
pearl: Calcium pyrophosphate crystals are rhomboid and weakly positively birefringent, while gout's are needle-shaped and strongly negative. Always aspirate a hot joint to rule out infection. Onset under 60 should prompt a metabolic work-up.

title: Lucid, then drowsy
context: A 24-year-old was hit on the side of the head, seemed fine for an hour, and is now increasingly drowsy.
question: What's the diagnosis?

img.author: James Heilman, MD
img.alt: Axial head CT with a bright lens-shaped collection under the skull, marked by a red arrow, and midline shift

hints: Look at the shape of the bright collection by the arrow.
It's lens-shaped, bulging inwards, and limited by the skull sutures.
why: A bright, biconvex (lens-shaped) collection under the skull on the patient's left, pressing on the brain and pushing the midline across. There is also a smaller bruise on the opposite side.
pearl: The classic source is the middle meningeal artery, torn by a fracture at the side of the skull. It can be fatal within hours but has a good outcome if evacuated quickly, so a falling GCS after head injury means urgent CT and neurosurgery.

title: Landed on the heels
context: A 38-year-old fell from a ladder and landed on both heels. One heel is badly swollen and bruised, and they can't stand.
question: What's the diagnosis?

img.author: Jojo
img.alt: Lateral X-ray of the foot and ankle with a crushed, irregular heel bone

hints: Look at the big bone at the back of the foot.
The heel bone has lost its shape and its internal lines are jumbled, as if it's been crushed.
why: Lateral foot X-ray showing a comminuted, flattened heel bone with a disrupted joint surface under the talus.
pearl: These are axial load injuries, so always examine the spine and the other heel: about 1 in 10 people also have a vertebral fracture. A reduced Böhler's angle can be the giveaway on subtler films, and CT guides treatment.

title: Waves of crying
context: A 9-month-old has waves of screaming with knees drawn up, vomiting, and lies pale and floppy between bouts.
question: What's the diagnosis?

img.file: Ultrasound of target sign in intussusception of the right bowel.png
img.author: Cerevisae (cropped)
img.alt: Abdominal ultrasound image with a round target of concentric rings of bowel

hints: This is an abdominal ultrasound. Look for a round structure, and what's inside it.
Concentric rings: a layer of bowel sliding inside another layer of bowel.
why: A target-shaped mass of concentric rings on bowel ultrasound: bowel telescoped inside bowel, usually near the junction of small and large bowel.
pearl: The textbook triad of colicky pain, vomiting and red-currant jelly stool appears in a minority, so a lethargic infant with episodic crying should raise suspicion. Most cases can be reduced with an air or contrast enema unless there's shock or perforation.

title: Sudden headache and weakness
context: A 69-year-old woman with poorly controlled high blood pressure has sudden headache, vomiting and arm weakness.
question: What's the diagnosis?

img.author: Glitzy queen00 at English Wikipedia
img.alt: Axial head CT with bright blood inside the brain and in the ventricles

hints: Is the bright area around the brain, or within it?
White blood sits within the brain tissue and has spilled into the ventricles.
why: Bright, fresh blood within the brain substance, tracking into the ventricular system, with blood layering in the back of the lateral ventricles.
pearl: Bleeding and clot strokes can look alike at the bedside, so CT comes first. Treatment aims to control blood pressure quickly and reverse any anticoagulant. Blood in the ventricles carries a worse outlook and can cause hydrocephalus.

title: Back pain on arching
context: A 16-year-old gymnast has low back pain that gets worse when arching backwards.
question: What's the diagnosis?

img.author: Lucien Monfils
img.alt: Lateral X-ray of the lower lumbar spine with an arrow where L5 has slipped forward on S1

hints: Line up the back edges of the lumbar vertebrae, going down to the sacrum.
The lowest lumbar vertebra has slipped forwards on the one beneath it.
why: Lateral lumbar X-ray with forward slippage of L5 on S1, marked by the arrow, breaking the smooth line of the back of the vertebrae.
pearl: Spondylolysis is a stress defect in the pars. If the vertebra then slips forwards, it becomes this diagnosis. It's common in gymnasts, divers and fast bowlers. Most settle with activity changes and rehab, and the highest-grade slips need specialist care.

title: Pain low on the left
context: A 61-year-old woman has three days of left lower abdominal pain, a fever and raised inflammatory markers.
question: What's the diagnosis?

img.author: Hellerhoff
img.alt: Axial CT of the pelvis with a red arrow near inflamed sigmoid colon

hints: Find the colon on the left side of the patient, which is on the right of the image, near the arrow.
There are small outpouchings of the bowel wall, with hazy inflamed fat around them.
why: Axial CT with contrast shows thickened sigmoid colon with diverticula and stranding of the fat around it. The arrow marks a small contained perforation and abscess.
pearl: Uncomplicated cases don't always need antibiotics. After a complicated episode, or if the colon hasn't been checked recently, colonoscopy about 6 weeks later helps exclude cancer, which can look similar on CT.

title: A nurse's groin pain
context: A 51-year-old nurse has had months of worsening left groin pain on walking, with no injury.
question: What's the diagnosis?

img.file: X-ray of pelvis with idiopathic avascular necrosis of the femoral head.jpg
img.author: Mikael Häggström
img.alt: Frontal X-ray of the pelvis with a dense, slightly flattened left femoral head

answer: Avascular necrosis of the femoral head
hints: Compare the two femoral heads: their roundness and density.
The left head is patchy, dense and starting to lose its smooth round contour.
why: The left femoral head shows patchy sclerosis and loss of its normal rounded contour, while the right looks normal. There's no major fracture.
pearl: X-rays can be normal early, so MRI is the test when pain persists. Causes include steroids, alcohol, sickle cell disease and trauma, though some cases are idiopathic. A subchondral crescent means the surface is collapsing.

title: Heart sounds on the right
context: A well 28-year-old has a pre-employment chest X-ray. The doctor hears the heart sounds best on the right.
question: What's the diagnosis?

img.author: Nevit
img.alt: Frontal chest X-ray with the heart and stomach gas on the patient's right side

hints: Check the side marker first, then find the apex of the heart and the stomach bubble.
The marker is correct, yet the heart's apex and the stomach gas are both on the patient's right.
why: The side marker is correct, yet the heart's apex and the gastric bubble are both on the patient's right. The organs are mirror-imaged, and the liver lies on the left.
pearl: About 1 in 4 people with complete mirror-image organs have primary ciliary dyskinesia, so ask about chronic sinus and chest infections. Most hearts are structurally normal. It's worth telling future doctors: appendicitis pain may be on the left.
